note: Hand-curated decode of the non-action BLE command handlers (D0/D1/D2/F0) and HID device-name binding. Offsets are payload offsets (image base 0). ABI names come from OpenWCH commit 64be9554615df522899579633530fd234d685682, EVT/EXAM/BLE/LIB/wchble_rom.h, matching the embedded CH32V20x_BLE_LIB_V1.3 string. Confidence labels: Confirmed (disassembly/ABI), Correlated (app/protocol behavior).
first_payload_byte: lbu a4, 0(s0)  (s0 = received BLE frame body pointer)

handlers.summary: Enable/select a per-connection notification stream. Requires first payload byte == 1, then calls the connection-slot status setter 0xb7c6 with selector a1=3.
evidence: 0xc060: lbu a4,0(s0); c.li a5,1; bne a4,a5 -> 0xbcba (reject unless byte==1)
0xc072: lbu reads an otherwise-unresolved RAM flag at 0x2000c7b0 before falling through to the D2 comparison

handlers.summary: Disable/teardown the notification stream selected by D0. Requires first payload byte == 1, then calls 0xb7c6 with selector a1=4, and returns via the unknown/no-reply tail 0xbcba.

Builds a D2 reply from a raw 12-byte record. Resident slot 0x40048 (tmos_memset) only zeroes the 8-byte reply buffer at sp+0x14. Local helper 0x28e copies internal record slot 4 into the 12-byte buffer at sp+0x20; the handler then assembles three adjacent byte pairs as big-endian halfwords and enqueues the reply through 0xd02.
evidence: 0xc08c: c.li a2,8; c.li a1,0; addi4spn a0,sp,0x14; c.jalr a5 (a5 = lw 0x48(0x40000)): memset(sp+0x14,0,8)
0xc094..0xc09a: jal 0x28e with a0=1,a1=4,a2=sp+0x20; 0x28e tail-calls tmos_memcpy at slot 0x4004c for a fixed 12-byte copy from internal record slot 4 to sp+0x20
0xc09e..0xc0d2: lbu/slli/or assembles three big-endian 16-bit words from bytes at sp+0x23..sp+0x28; the final two reply bytes remain zero
0xc0d8: jal 0xd02 with a0=connection handle, a1=0xd2, a2=sp+0x14, a3=8

handlers.summary: Configuration/provisioning write. Rejects sub-code s3 <= 0xD (bgeu guard), validates a 14-byte credential/name via 0x12d4 (byte-compare against an expected 14-byte buffer), and on success forwards (s3-0xE) entries starting at frame+0xE to the config worker 0xa39a.
evidence: 0xc0f8: jal 0x12d4 with a1=0xe (14-byte compare/validate); bnez a0 -> reject

helpers.0x12d4: 14-byte buffer validate: builds expected buffer via 0x129c, compares frame bytes 0..13; returns 0 on match.
helpers.0xa39a: config worker: stores a 16-bit handle, then dispatches on (payload[0]-1) through a 7-entry jump table (range-checked bltu 6) into config-RAM writers.

hid_name_binding.resident_compare_slot: 0x4003c (tmos_memcmp; loaded as lw a5,0(s6) or lw a5,0x3c(0x40000))
hid_name_binding.summary: On GAP discovery/connect the firmware compares the peer device name against a fixed list of keyboard identities to pick which HID profile to emulate / which peer to bind. Each comparison calls tmos_memcmp, whose ABI returns TRUE for equality: zero continues to the next candidate and nonzero selects the matching profile.
evidence: 0x99ca: auipc/addi a0 -> 0x11604 ('BT KeyBoard'); c.li a2,0xb; jalr resident cmp
0x9a50: a0 -> 0x11620 ('MINI_KEYBOARD'); c.li a2,0xd; jalr resident cmp
0x9a68: a0 -> 0x11630 ('BLE-M3'); c.li a2,6; jalr resident cmp
0x9a5c: lui s6,0x40 sets s6=0x00040000; lw a5,0x3c(s6) reloads the resident compare pointer
